newsitem.title: NIGERIA: 28 foreigners freed in Nigeria, still two hostages.
newsitem.headline: 28 foreigners freed in Nigeria, still two hostages.

text.p: Twenty-eight foreigners held hostage on an offshore barge by Nigerian workers demanding pay rises were freed but two other Frenchmen remained prisoners on another ship, the barge captain said on Saturday.

"All the expatriates were led off the boat at 8.15 (1915 GMT) last night," Tabang Cora, the Filipino captain of the barge WB-82 said from a hotel in Calabar, southeastern Nigeria, where they were being lodged.
"We are very tired but we are well," he told Reuters.
The hostages, held for five days before being released, were all foreigners - 10 Filipinos, nine Frenchmen, five Indians, two Britons, one Lebanese and one Belgian.
But Cora said two other Frenchmen were being held on a vessel called American Pride, not far from the WB-82, by workers who were also demanding higher wages.
The WB-82's group had been held on the barge about 30 miles offshore from the oil-producing town of Eket since December 23 by 60 Nigerian workers.
Earlier the Philippine embassy consul-general in Lagos, Hermes Dorado, said the Nigerians had been taken by the navy to its base but Cora said some Nigerians were still on the barge.
"There are still negotiations going on about the salaries but I don't know the details," he added.
The dispute involved a French oil services company identified as NTPM that employed the workers on its barge WB-82, which transports crude oil from onshore fields to tankers.
The Nigerians were not armed and had not carried out threats to harm the foreigners if their demands were not met by Thursday.
Mobil Nigeria Unlimited, a joint venture with the U.S. firm Mobil Corp, is the main producer of crude oil in the area. A Mobil official said the company was not involved in the incident.
